crescent-star.context: A crescent moon beside a five-pointed star. Used for Islamic and Muslim content, mosque and prayer time apps, Ramadan and Eid greetings, and faith or religion filters.

cross-christian.context: A Latin cross with a longer lower arm. Used for Christian and church content, faith and religion filters, Easter and Sunday service listings, and places of worship on maps.

dharma-wheel.context: An eight-spoked wheel with a hub, the dharmachakra of Buddhist teaching. Used for Buddhist temples and content, meditation and mindfulness apps, and faith or religion filters.

hamsa.context: An open hand with a thumb on each side and an eye in the palm. Used for protection and good luck charms, jewellery and amulets, Middle Eastern and North African culture, and spiritual content.

khanda.context: The Khanda: a double-edged sword standing through a ring, flanked by two curved swords that cross below. Used for Sikh content, gurdwara listings, Vaisakhi greetings and faith or religion filters.

om.context: The Om symbol, written as the sacred syllable in Devanagari with a crescent and dot above. Used for Hindu content and temples, yoga and meditation apps, mantras and spiritual practice.

peace-sign.context: A circle with a vertical line and two lines angled down from its centre, the peace symbol. Used for peace and anti-war messages, protests and activism, 1960s and hippie themes, and calm or harmony designs.

prayer-beads.context: A loop of beads with one larger bead and a tassel hanging below. Used for prayer and meditation apps, counting recitations, rosary, mala or tasbih content, and spiritual practice.

star-of-david.context: The Star of David: two overlapping equilateral triangles forming a six-pointed star. Used for Jewish and Judaism content, synagogue listings, Jewish holidays and faith or religion filters.

torii.context: A torii gate with two pillars, a curved top lintel and a straight crossbeam below. Used for Shinto shrines, Japan travel guides and maps, Japanese culture content and temple or shrine listings.

yin-yang.context: A circle split by an S-shaped curve into two halves, each holding a dot of the opposite side. Used for balance and harmony themes, Taoism and Chinese philosophy, martial arts, and wellness or meditation apps.
